main_body: Three-tier shelf rack of thin grey slabs with small candles on each tier and a dark open frame beneath the bottom tier
top_band: none: each tier is a 2-3 row light grey strip (rows ~14-15, 20-21, 24-25) that reads as a front edge/rim, not a surface seen from above
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: candle tips and cream wax, then a 1-row light grey edge, then 2 rows of mid grey, and then the next tier. The shelves are thin horizontal strips with no foreshortened top surface, so they read as front-on planks. The lower section is an open dark frame with a thin dark bar, and no top band is visible. Candles sit on a line rather than on a surface. This is a front elevation with only edge lines for tops, and the top is a rim of 1-2px.

style.evidence: The shelf slabs use about 3 grey tones (light edge, mid, dark) with no grain or speckle. The candles are tiny, with 2-4 tones each. The lower frame is a flat dark fill with a neutral dark outline. Compared with the richly textured stall and well references, it is clearly thinner and flatter, with low colour counts per tile.
